**STEP 1 - Scene:** A hospital-style tray meal photographed from the front at about 35 degrees above the table. It has roasted chicken, mixed vegetables, fruit, a glass of juice, and a bottle of a brown drink. A tray label reads 3079.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The paper plates and bowls are the only vessels. I'll size them by eye against the tray: chicken plate ~22 cm diameter (area ~380 cm²), fruit bowl ~16 cm (area ~200 cm²), vegetable bowl ~13 cm (area ~133 cm²).

**STEP 3 - Items:** Roasted chicken (sliced, with some browned skin), mixed fruit (strawberries, orange and pineapple-type chunks), mixed vegetables (sweet corn, carrot, peas, broccoli), apple-type juice, and a brown milky drink (likely coffee or tea with milk).

**STEP 4 - Area:** Chicken covers ~45% of the plate (~170 cm²). Fruit covers ~70% of its bowl (~140 cm²). Vegetables cover ~60% of their bowl (~80 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Chicken ~170 cm² × 1 cm ≈ 170 ml. Fruit ~140 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 350 ml. Vegetables ~80 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 160 ml. The drinks are estimated by visible fill level, about 200 ml juice and 150 ml brown drink.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Chicken 170 ml × 0.9 ≈ 155 g. Fruit 350 ml × 0.6 ≈ 210 g. Vegetables 160 ml × 0.6 ≈ 96 g. Juice ≈ 200 g. Brown drink ≈ 150 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Chicken ~180 kcal/100 g gives ~280 kcal. Fruit ~40 kcal/100 g gives ~84 kcal. Vegetables ~50 kcal/100 g gives ~48 kcal. Juice ~45 kcal/100 g gives ~90 kcal. Brown drink ~40 kcal/100 g gives ~60 kcal. Total ≈ 560 kcal from about 810 g.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A roughly 150 g chicken portion, a fruit bowl of about 200 g, a small vegetable side, and two drinks is plausible for a single tray meal. The drink values are the least certain because the fill levels and contents are hard to judge from the photo.
